topic: Blue sky and red sunset are the same trick

claims.claim: Air molecules (N2, O2) are much smaller than visible wavelengths (~1000x per NOAA) and scatter short wavelengths more (Rayleigh scattering, intensity ~ 1/lambda^4).
Blue (~450 nm) is scattered about 4x more than red (~650 nm). (650/450)^4 = 4.35; 3.7x for 625 nm.
At sunrise/sunset light crosses far more atmosphere (Brailey Sims estimate ~30x more than overhead), so blue is scattered out of the direct beam and orange/red remain.
The blue removed from a sunset beam contributes to the blue sky seen elsewhere ('sunsets are red because the daytime sky is blue').
sources: https://weather.metoffice.gov.uk/learn-about/weather/optical-effects/why-is-the-sky-blue ('same scattering process, seen from different angles')

note: Atmosphere thickness in the diagram is exaggerated for readability; on-screen label says 'dozens x more air', matching the ~30x estimate. Violet nuance omitted for length.
